In [[mathematics]], '''Buchsbaum rings''' are Noetherian [[local ring]]s such that every [[system of parameters]] is a weak sequence.
A sequence <math>(a_1,\cdots,a_r)</math> of the maximal ideal <math>m</math> is called a weak sequence if <math> m\cdot((a_1,\cdots,a_{i-1})\colon
a_i)\subset(a_1,\cdots,a_{i-1})</math> for all <math>i</math>.

They were introduced by {{harvs|txt | last1=Stückrad | first1=Jürgen | last2=Vogel | first2=Wolfgang | | year=1973 }} and are named after [[David Buchsbaum]].

Every [[Cohen–Macaulay ring|Cohen–Macaulay local ring]] is a Buchsbaum ring. Every Buchsbaum ring is a [[generalized Cohen–Macaulay ring]].
